task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can a change in the offensive five be detected as a shift in shot mix from play-by-play data?
Does the shot-mix shift survive shooter-level and lineup-level controls, or is it a shooter-selection artifact?
What exposure (number of lineup-change events) is needed to detect a plausible shot-mix difference?
Does the same-shooter or other-play-type placebo show that the design separates personnel effects from artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: On a PULL_UP exposure-effect analysis, the slope was -0.0255 with lineup fixed effects and -0.0063 without them. A same-shooter placebo on other play types gave -0.0071 to -0.0075, which [prior work] reads as consistent with a shooter-level confound. [prior work] says its sample and power were not recorded.

A reproduced selection-based excess of 0.4080 (CI [0.378, 0.438]) was matched by a within-unit permutation null (0.3798 vs 0.3744, z 0.40), so [prior work] reads the excess as mechanical under the selection rule. Drift-centring removed the tail asymmetry. [prior work] notes limits from drift, insufficient exposure, and selection or regression to the mean.

On POST_UP then PUTBACK stacking, stacked suppression (-0.071, n=1,047) was smaller than either component alone and far below the additive prediction (-0.232). One cluster gradient had an unexpected sign, and per-player stacked n was often under 5. [prior work] cites an implementation-bug limit and a small-sample limit.

A penalty-state pilot (3 to 4 team fouls, clock above 2:30, game x offense x period FE) found the penalty contrast was not distinct from the 2-to-3 and 4-to-5+ placebo contrasts. Standard errors were not printed. [prior work]'s verdict field reads null, and its sample and power were not recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a play-type-specific decline with exposure to defensive adaptation, without a same-shooter placebo on other play types.
failed_approaches.why: The effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup fixed effects were dropped, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was of similar size (-0.0071/-0.0075), which [prior work] reads as a shooter-level confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a selected large-drop unit compared with matched controls as evidence of an effect.
failed_approaches.why: A within-unit permutation null reproduced the excess (z 0.40), so [prior work] reads it as mechanical under the selection rule; regression to the mean and drift were also flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Additive stacking of two opponent shot-type suppressions against a star possession.
failed_approaches.why: Observed stacked suppression (-0.071) was far below the additive prediction (-0.232); per-player stacked n was often under 5, and [prior work] cites an implementation-bug limit.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a penalty-state behaviour change against adjacent-foul placebos.
failed_approaches.why: The penalty contrast was not distinct from the placebo contrasts, and standard errors were not printed; [prior work] classes the mechanism as unclear.

evidence_establishes: In records from this project, a lineup-fixed-effects or same-shooter placebo was the check that separated a real exposure-linked effect from a shooter or lineup confound ([prior work][prior work]).
Permutation nulls and matched-control comparisons under a selection rule can reproduce an apparent excess with no personnel effect ([prior work][prior work]).
Placebo contrasts were needed before a state-change effect could be judged, and in the pilot the placebos were not separable from the effect ([prior work][prior work]).
Retrieval returned no record that tests offensive-five changes against shot mix directly, so the question's own premise is unconfirmed by earlier work.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing one player in the offensive five moves shot mix in the 2022-23 to 2024-25 NBA data.
Whether the design can detect a personnel effect of a given size: no power or detectability calculation was retrieved.
Any shot-mix effect size, lineup-level estimate, or matchup effect for this data.
Whether the retrieved records' data, sample sizes, or pipelines match the stated data sources.
own_inferences: The question as posed is partly circular: it presumes the design can detect personnel effects and uses that presumption as its conclusion. A positive result would validate the design but would not by itself show a specific personnel effect, so the question should be split into a detectability (power or simulation) claim and an effect-estimate claim.

The lineup-fixed-effects versus shooter-level confound pattern in [prior work][prior work] suggests that a lineup-change contrast may be driven by who shoots, not by who is on court, unless the shooter is held fixed.

Shot mix is a plausible outcome because shot distance and type are recorded per shot, but the fraction of changes that are clean personnel swaps (rather than changes with game-state or fatigue shifts) is unknown.

Derived play-type records from [source] database could be affected by the same labelling risks that [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] point to, if the labels are built from the outcome.
uncertainties: No retrieved record used the stated data sources or the offensive-five question. All four records concern other outcomes (PULL_UP decline, suppression excess, POST_UP/PUTBACK stacking, penalty state), so their conclusions transfer only by analogy.
Sample sizes and power are NOT_RECORDED for [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work], and FAM:[prior work] gives per-player stacked n under 5.
Season-to-season drift across 2022-23 to 2024-25 was flagged in [prior work][prior work] but not quantified for this question.
The number of offensive-five changes per team-game and the share that are single-player swaps are not stated in the data description.
Whether the 2025 data fully reflects the regular season and playoffs is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: Earlier records showed that unmatched lineup or shooter contrasts can produce an apparent effect that falls away under placebos ([prior work][prior work]) and that selected-unit comparisons can reproduce an excess under permutation nulls ([prior work][prior work]). These pushed the decision away from a direct test of the premise and toward a design with same-shooter and other-player placebos, a power analysis first, and a restriction to clean single-player swaps. This is an inference from [prior work]' patterns, not a conclusion any record reaches about this question.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup changes co-occur with game state, opponent, fatigue, and shooter identity; without a shooter-fixed design, shot-mix shifts cannot be attributed to personnel ([prior work][prior work]).
No power calculation was retrieved, and per-lineup shot counts may be too low to detect modest shot-mix differences (FAM:[prior work] notes per-player n under 5 in a related design).
A positive result relies on placebo contrasts that have failed to separate effect from artifact in related records ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. The four records address related but different questions (PULL_UP exposure, selection-based suppression excess, opponent stacking, penalty-state behaviour). They are relied on only for their design lessons: shooter-fixed placebos, permutation nulls for selected units, and power reporting.

risks.text: Shot mix varies with shooter, game state, opponent, and fatigue at the time of a lineup change, so a raw shot-mix shift is not attributable to personnel.
A shooter-level or lineup-level confound can produce an apparent effect that disappears under a same-shooter placebo, as in [prior work][prior work].
Per-lineup and per-shooter shot counts may be too small for a stable shot-mix estimate.
Clean single-player swaps may be too rare in the 2022-23 to 2024-25 data to support a stable estimate, and the playoff sample is smaller still.
Selecting on a large shot-mix shift and comparing it to matched controls can reproduce the excess mechanically, as in [prior work][prior work].
Shot-mix tendencies change across seasons, so pooling 2022-23 to 2024-25 can confound season trend with personnel.
The base rate of clean single-player offensive-five swaps is not reported, so the achievable sample size and detectable effect are unknown.
Testing many shot-type and distance categories, and many lineup pairs, raises false-positive risk without correction.
Shot-distance and shot-type labels, and derived play-type records, may be misclassified, which would bias the shot-mix outcome.

design.estimand: Within-team, within-game change in the share of shot attempts at each distance and type (rim, midrange, corner three, above-break three) when a single named player enters or exits the offensive five, holding the other four players and the shooter fixed, relative to placebo swaps that do not change the shooter's on-court status.
design.unit: Stint-level observation: a shooter-by-stint record of attempts, nested within game and team, defined by a single-player swap in the offensive five.
design.sample: Regular-season 2022-23 and 2023-24 for estimation, with 2024-25 regular season held out for confirmation. Playoffs kept as a separate sensitivity sample. Restrict to clean single-player swaps with at least a minimum shot count per stint (threshold to be fixed before analysis).
design.power: Before analysis, run a simulation calibrated to observed swap counts and shot counts to find the minimum detectable shot-mix shift at 80% power. Proceed only if the minimum detectable shift is judged useful for the question. Report the simulated detectable effect and the achieved sample size.
design.controls: Shooter fixed effects; game x offense x period fixed effects; score margin and clock bins; opponent defensive matchup minutes as a covariate; substitution-interval fatigue proxy (minutes since last substitution); shot-clock bin. Compare lineup-fixed-effect and no-lineup-fixed-effect specifications and report both, as in [prior work][prior work].
design.falsification: Use same-shooter placebo swaps (shooter unchanged, other four unchanged), other-player placebo swaps, and a non-shot outcome such as turnover rate on the same stints. Treat a shot-mix shift that appears in placebos at a similar size as an artifact ([prior work][prior work]). Include a permutation null that reassigns swap timing within game, to check for mechanical selection ([prior work][prior work]).
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary outcome (share of attempts at the rim, or a pre-specified three-category shot mix). Correct secondary distance and type categories and lineup pairs for multiple testing (e.g. Holm or FDR), and report corrected intervals.
design.decision_rule: The question is supported only if (a) the primary shot-mix shift is nonzero with a CI excluding zero after correction, (b) it exceeds both same-shooter and other-player placebo shifts, (c) it holds in the 2024-25 holdout with the same sign, and (d) the simulation shows the design could have detected a shift of the size observed. If the placebos match the effect, record artifact. If power is inadequate, record untestable rather than null.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, as listed in the data description; substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, and play-by-play shot distance and result. Derived play-type records from [source] database are excluded from the primary outcome to avoid outcome-derived labels; they may be used only in a sensitivity analysis.
